question: How do the cycle references Raffray et al. 2008 (ARIES-CS engineering design, Fusion Sci. Technol. 54, 725) cite for the Brayton power cycle represent heat delivery from the blanket-helium, PbLi and divertor-helium loops to the cycle helium: one lumped heater or per-branch exchangers, with what terminal or approach temperature, what cycle inlet and outlet temperatures, and what duties; and does that representation resolve the inconsistency among the published branch duties (1192 / 1444 / 186 MW), temperature spans (helium 386 to 456 C, PbLi 451 to 738 C, divertor 573 to 700 C, cycle 355 to 707 C) and the series-then-parallel arrangement of Raffray Fig. 12? The cited references are Ref. 15, R. Schleicher, A. R. Raffray, C. P. Wong, An Assessment of the Brayton Cycle for High Performance Power Plant, Fusion Technol. 39, 823 (2001), attached on p735 to the three-compression-stage single-expansion cycle, and Ref. 13, X. Wang, S. Malang, A. R. Raffray, Modular Dual Coolant Pb-17Li Blanket Design for ARIES-CS Compact Stellarator Power Plant, Proc. 20th IEEE SOFE, Knoxville, 2005, attached on p732 to the blanket coupled to a Brayton power cycle.
where_to_look: Fusion Technology (ANS, Taylor and Francis) volume 39 page 823, 2001, Schleicher Raffray Wong Brayton cycle assessment
UCSD ARIES program report library (aries.ucsd.edu, cer.ucsd.edu, ARIES-AT and ARIES-CS power core and Brayton cycle reports by Raffray, Schleicher, Wong, Wang, Malang)
IEEE Xplore 20th IEEE/NPSS Symposium on Fusion Engineering 2005, Wang Malang Raffray modular dual coolant Pb-17Li blanket ARIES-CS
OSTI.gov and Google Scholar for author-posted copies of either reference
